prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1305; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision on a two-lane road. Both vehicles were drivable and towed from the scene. Claimant reports neck stiffness and lower back soreness. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Liability questions pending police report.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes neck strain with limited rotation and a dull ache in the lower back that worsened the following morning. Claimant has not yet seen a physician and was advised to get evaluated and keep all treatment records. Collision statement recorded.

Entry 3: Obtained the responding officer's report. Report notes light front-end damage to both vehicles, airbags not deployed, and no citations issued at the scene. Other driver's statement is consistent with claimant's account of a slow approach and minor impact. Liability appears shared pending further review.

Entry 4: Claimant provided medical intake forms from urgent care showing diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain with prescribed muscle relaxants and physical therapy referral. Claimant confirmed no prior neck or back claims. Photos of both vehicles reviewed and filed.

Entry 5: Sent claimant written explanation of coverage options, including medical payments and rental reimbursement, and reminded claimant of the right to seek independent legal advice. Claimant acknowledged receipt. Reserve set for bodily injury and property damage. File remains open pending treatment updates and repair estimates.
